key_insight: Combining sky images with time-series in a bidirectional multimodal LLM framework improves solar forecasting, especially when clouds drive rapid irradiance and PV power changes.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve short-term PV and GHI forecasting for dispatch and reserve scheduling, while reducing dependence on large site-specific datasets.
method: Align sky-image patches with time-series patches.
Fuse both modalities through bidirectional multimodal fusion into a unified representation.
Map the fused embedding into an LLM for final forecasting.
evidence_signal: On the SIRTA and SKIPP'D datasets, the method outperformed all baselines across forecasting horizons, with up to 25.4% relative MSE reduction and strong gains under cloudy conditions and few-shot settings.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the availability and quality of synchronized sky imagery, so deployment may be sensitive to sensor placement, calibration, and missing image data.
paper_title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
